risks: The 400,000-byte cap in studio/mcp/fetch.py defeats three of the eight useful channels and NONE of them can be paged (Google's Veo page, Runway's 520 KB openapi.json, OpenAI's openapi.yaml). This section cannot fully read a vendor OpenAPI spec today. Either the cap gets a range-request or streaming mode, or those sources stay partial and every claim from them carries `partial_document` forever. Raising the cap is a change to a module this section does not own (Ц2) — it is a request, not a task.

Deployment-qualified ids (`veo-3.1@fal.ai`) change how every consumer of the base looks a model up. Done carelessly this fragments the base worse than the current five-ids-for-one-Veo mess. scripts/merge_model_ids.py must own the bare-id side and `underlying()` must be the only way anything joins them.

The known-paths table for open-weight inference configs (Wan: wan/configs/__init__.py) is per-lab and hand-maintained. It will be wrong for the next lab and silently empty for most — the gate must make 'no structural spec found' a loud could-not-measure, not a quiet skip, or coverage will look better than it is. Ц10 applies: no config path enters the table without a fetch proving it exists (Wan2.2's config.json guess already returned 404).

Value-diff re-reading every spec claim is N fetches per run against hosts with rate limits and, in Google's case, a 400 KB page each time. This has to be budgeted and staged (HF `sha` first, full re-read only on change), or the staleness gate becomes the thing people disable.

Rate limits and end-of-life are the weakest two attributes in the whole section. Rate limits: the one vendor page I probed does not carry them in HTML at all (0 'Tier 1' hits). EOL: the base has exactly 1 `lifecycle` row today, and open-weight models have no EOL concept at all. Do not promise these two; report them as thin.

Prices on model cards are frequently third-party prices repeated by the vendor — Kokoro's card cites artificialanalysis.ai and deepinfra.com, and artificialanalysis.ai is on this environment's refused list. A price recorded from a vendor card can therefore be a blog-grade number wearing a vendor URL. Price rows need the cited-source host recorded in the note, and the tier taken from the CITED host where the card is plainly quoting.

Section 1 — The model range: how the bas.target_state: DONE is not "knows every model". DONE is: for each of six declared slices (text-to-video, image-to-video, text-to-image, text-to-speech, text-generation on Hugging Face, plus closed hosted models), the base holds a canonical id and at least one read, tiered fact for every repo that passes the published selection rule, and a nightly job proves the number. The rule, stated so it can be checked: an HF repo enters the candidate set if likes >= 25 in its pipeline_tag slice AND it carries none of the tags base_model:adapter / base_model:quantized / base_model:merge. MEASURED today on text-to-video: 162 repos are at likes>=25, 45 of them are derivatives, so the slice is 117 models — and the base currently answers for 8 of them (bare-name match against the 231 ids). Target for that slice is 117/117 candidates DISCOVERED and canonicalised, with promotion to facts human-approved, not 117/117 facts invented. Closed hosted models are a separate, smaller target: the 3365-entry litellm snapshot filtered to mode in {chat, image_generation, video_generation} and to providers whose vendor page is readable — every such id gets a canonical spelling and a deprecation_date watch. KNOWINGLY OUT OF SCOPE, and it must be written in the README rather than discovered later: LoRAs and adapters, GGUF/AWQ/FP8/INT4 repacks, merges, community finetunes below the likes floor, and any model whose only description is a resell listing. Those are recorded as ALIASES OF or DERIVATIVES OF a base model, never as models with their own capability claims.

risks: The closed-LLM half rests on ONE source. models.dev and llm-stats.com are both refused, so the litellm snapshot has no independent cross-check; a wrong context window there enters the base uncontradicted and looks settled. Mitigation is honest labelling (portal tier, pinned sha) plus an allowlist ask for one second catalogue — but until that ask is granted, this is a stated weakness, not a solved problem.

fetch.py returns no response headers, so HF paging currently depends on a parameter HF has already deprecated in writing. When the remaining skip window closes, discovery stops at whatever depth still answers — and it will stop QUIETLY, returning fewer rows rather than an error. The coverage floor gate is the only thing that would catch it, which is why that gate's truncation negative-control matters more than the rest.

base_model:finetune is genuinely ambiguous and it is 207 of 931 rows in the video slice — 22%. Routing all of them to 'undecidable' creates a human queue that could be larger than the kept set. If nobody works that queue, real models (Wan2.2-Lightning, FusioniX) sit outside the base indefinitely and the coverage number looks healthy while missing them.

The likes floor is a CHOSEN constant (ВЫБРАНО: 25, by me, from the measured distribution 500->16, 200->32, 100->57, 50->93, 25->162), not a measured one. It is defensible on the video slice and probably wrong for text-to-speech, where the whole field is smaller. Per-slice floors will be needed and each must be re-measured, not copied.

Promotion is the bottleneck by design, and design bottlenecks get routed around under time pressure. The failure mode is somebody adding a --auto flag to promote_candidates.py; the import-boundary test in gate 4 is what makes that show up in a diff instead of in the base.

Hugging Face is itself a portal, so a vendor claim about an open-weights model still needs the vendor's own page — and for several of the top ids the vendor page host is one the policy refuses. Expect a class of models that can be DISCOVERED and canonicalised but can only ever hold portal-tier facts, and say so in the coverage report rather than letting portal rows accumulate as if they were vendor ones.
Section 1 — The model range: how the bas.effort: Roughly 6-8 agent-sessions. What dominates is not the code: hf_catalogue.py, derivative.py and discover_models.py are two sessions together, and closed_llm.py plus the pinned snapshot is half of one. The cost is (a) identity.py and its alias table — merge_model_ids.py took a whole session for 5 collisions, and the alias table for six slices is the same work at ~50x the row count, spread over two sessions with a human ruling on the finetune cases; (b) the promotion queue, which is human-paced and does not compress: 117 candidates in one slice at the current read-and-quote rate is not one sitting, and the plan should state a per-week promotion rate rather than a completion date; (c) the fetch.py header change, which is small but belongs to another writer (Ц2) and so costs a handoff rather than an edit. Stop-condition to write down before starting (Ц9): if by the fourth session the text-to-video slice is not at 117/117 discovered and 40+ promoted, stop and record which of the three — cursor paging, the finetune ambiguity, or the promotion rate — was the binding constraint, with the number."

Section 3 — Applicability in the communi.section: Section 3 — Applicability in the community: what people actually get out of these models
Section 3 — Applicability in the communi.target_state: The base can answer "what do practitioners actually get out of model X, and where does it stop working for them" with rows checkable the same way every other row is: a quoted piece of evidence, a URL, a tier decided by that URL, three outcomes. Done means: (1) community material is split into EVIDENCE (an artefact — a prompt with the image it produced and its parameters, or a practitioner report naming settings AND observed outcome, quoted verbatim), VOLUME (downloads/likes/stars — not evidence, separate ledger, attribute names prefixed `adoption.`, structurally unable to enter model_facts.jsonl or corroborate a capability claim), and OPINION (no settings, no artefact — not recorded, counted as dropped); (2) nothing here writes model_facts.jsonl unattended — collectors write a dated harvest file and a human runs scripts/ingest_harvest.py, which already refuses a quote-less row (MIN_EVIDENCE_CHARS=12) and a tier disagreeing with the URL (studio/mcp/advice.py:540-560 via source_hosts.classify); (3) repetition never becomes weight — ten people repeating each other stay one source and count is never an argument on a contested attribute; (4) the slice is bounded: open-weight models with a Hugging Face repo plus Civitai checkpoints, with closed API models (Kling, Veo, Sora, Runway) knowingly OUT because they have no HF discussion tab and the practitioner channel for them returned 403 today.

build.does: Collector for Hugging Face discussion threads. Pure functions plus one fetch door. `thread_refs(listing_payload)` turns a discussions page into refs carrying num, title, numComments, createdAt, author, numReactionUsers and repoOwner.isParticipating — so a thread with 0 comments is skipped WITHOUT a request, exactly the way civitai.version_refs uses hasPositivePrompt. `reports_from_thread(payload, ref)` walks events[].data.latest.raw and returns the house judging dict (outcome/checked/violations/unmeasured/note) plus rows, counting separately what was dropped: `no_settings` (prose with no named parameter, node, resolution, seed or error string), `duplicate_text` (see the shingle rule below), `not_english` — identifiedLanguage.probability is on every event and 1 of the 6 events measured in thread 44 was Spanish. Each row carries model, attribute (failure_mode / limitation / working_configuration), the verbatim quote, source_url, provenance `hf:<author.name>`, `is_org_member`, and harvested date. It does NOT decide a tier and does NOT write the base.

risks: THE BRIEF'S LICENCE PREMISE IS WRONG, AND THE REAL CLAUSE IS STRICTER. The brief says the repository gitignores its Civitai corpus "over that site's clause 2(d)". Measured: the .gitignore comment cites THIS repository's own LICENCE clause 2(d) — "reuse the prompts, prompt fragments, directive strings, calibrated thresholds and measured constants contained here" — the worry being that publishing other people's prompts inside a repo whose licence claims rights over its prompts would assert a claim over their work. Civitai's own binding clause is different and sharper: ToS §6.1 grants access "solely for your personal, non-commercial use". This is a commercial studio project. Consequence for the design: Civitai contributes prompt/parameter artefacts to the PRIVATE corpus only (the existing gitignored civitai_prompts.jsonl path), and no Civitai-sourced quote may enter the published model_facts.jsonl. The public base's community evidence comes from Hugging Face discussions. Whether that is licensed for quotation is НЕПРОВЕРЕНО and is a question for the owner before the first publish, not for me.

REDDIT IS SHUT AND source_hosts.py DOES NOT KNOW IT. PORTAL_SOURCES lists reddit.com/r/comfyui/ and old.reddit.com/r/comfyui/ with a comment arguing why a workflow subreddit earns the middle rung; today that host answers 403 (site-level, denied:false — NOT an egress refusal, and not to be routed around). The table is a rung table, not a reachability map, and it says so — but a plan reading it as a channel list would have budgeted a week on an unreadable source.

POPULARITY COUNTERS ARE NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS AGES, AND THE MISTAKE IS SILENT. downloads 745 vs downloadsAllTime 53419 on the same repo. Any ranking that mixes the two, or that compares a 2024 model's 30-day window with a 2026 model's, produces a confident wrong answer. Mitigation: `window` is a mandatory field in the adoption ledger; a row without it cannot be written.

LIKES AND DOWNLOADS ARE PER REPO, NOT PER MODEL VERSION. LTX-2.3 (1843 likes, 1392095 downloads) and LTX-2.5 (1942, 912729) are separate repos, but Wan and Flux publish several versions inside one repo. Attributing an adoption number to a base model id needs merge_model_ids.py and will still be approximate; say so on the row rather than pretending precision.

SELF-PROMOTION AND ASTROTURF LOOK LIKE REPORTS. Measured titles in the same 45-thread listing include "LTX 2.5 Just Changed Local AI Video Forever!" and "LTX 2.5 on RTX 3060: Impressive Speed & Quality Out of the Box", both by the same author, alongside genuine multi-day test writeups. The artefact rule (a named setting AND an observed outcome) is what separates them, and it will misclassify in both directions; the drop counts printed per run are what makes that visible instead of invisible.

A VENDOR EMPLOYEE ANSWERING IN A THREAD IS STILL A COMMUNITY URL. The measured reply ("the dubbing pipeline ... is currently still optimized for LTX 2.3") is a genuine vendor statement about applicability, but it sits on huggingface.co, which classifies portal. Promoting it to vendor requires a human adding huggingface.co/Lightricks/ to VENDOR_SOURCES — which is correct and should stay manual, at the cost that real vendor statements sit one rung low until somebody edits the table.

CIVITAI PAGES ARE ENORMOUS AND THE 400000-BYTE CAP IS CLOSE. limit=3 returned 376557 bytes. A collector that raises the limit will truncate mid-JSON exactly the way the ComfyUI-Manager custom-node-list.json already does. The listing must stay at limit<=3 and the run must budget pages explicitly.

THE LISTING AND THE VERSION ENDPOINT DISAGREE ON HOW MANY IMAGES EXIST (16 advertised, 10 returned). Nothing in the current collector notices. It is small, but it is the shape of the defect that killed /api/v1/images: a counter that says one thing and a payload that does another.

Section 6 — Assembling a stack for a pro.section: Section 6 — Assembling a stack for a product task: the reasoning layer, and the loop that proves it
Section 6 — Assembling a stack for a pro.target_state:
Given a written brief, the layer emits ONE artefact — a Stack Proposal — that is checkable line by line:

(a) every constraint it derived, printed next to the verbatim words of the brief it came from. A constraint with no quoted brief text is refused, the same way ingest_harvest.py refuses a fact with no quoted evidence.
(b) for each slot (plate ingest / presenter / lip-sync / audio / join) the surviving candidates, and for every ELIMINATED candidate the exact fact row — model, attribute, value, source_url, tier, read_directly — that killed it. Elimination with an empty evidence list is a build failure, not a low-confidence answer.
(c) a silence ledger: the count of deciding constraints the base could not answer for the winner. Non-zero silence forbids the verdict "pass"; the proposal comes back "could not measure" and names what is missing. MEASURED baseline: the blind evaluation is 114 questions, 50 silent (43.9%), 17 contested, 5 wrong, 42 answered — so most briefs will legitimately land on "could not measure" on day one, and that is the correct output, not a defect to be smoothed.
(d) one filed measurement proposal per silent deciding attribute, through the EXISTING studio/mcp/proposal.py (gap / test / cost_usd / cost_basis / decides). The layer never fills a silence with a guess and never approves its own spend.
(e) the word UNPROVEN stamped on it until a run record exists for it in studio/knowledge/stack_runs.jsonl carrying a machine score, an artefact path, and a human's one-line note on what they saw. Today that count is 0 for every prompt in this package; the honest starting state of this section is that every proposal it can emit is UNPROVEN.

Done = scripts/stack_eval.py runs a frozen brief set and prints `briefs N / proposed M / proved P / could-not-measure K`, with P > 0 — i.e. at least one stack has been proposed, run, looked at, and recorded.

SCOPE LINE, stated honestly. Coverable: briefs whose deciding constraints fall in the six attribute families the base actually populates — duration (56 rows / 38 models), price (88 / 81), resolution (45 / 37), licence (18 / 16), identity-holding (27 / 14), aspect ratio (15 / 13). Knowingly OUT of scope: aesthetic judgement ("does it feel premium"), anything the base has no attribute for, and any slot where the base holds only class-level findings (171 of them) rather than model-level rows — class findings inform the RISK section of a proposal, never an elimination.

At 43.9% silence most briefs will honestly terminate in 'could not measure', and a layer that mostly says 'I don't know' will be pressured into loosening. That pressure is the real threat to this section, not a bug. The counter-pressure is the measurement-proposal queue: the layer's output when it cannot answer is a costed, approvable question, and queue length is the metric that makes the silence productive instead of embarrassing.

Closing the loop costs money and a human, every cycle. The lip-sync slot is cheap ($0.20 flat up to 40s at fal's published rate, read this run) but the presenter/plate slot is not, and a 15-second vertical video generation is the expensive half. Realistically this loop closes a few times a month, not a few times a day, so the run log will be small for a long time and must not be averaged into confident-looking rates.

fal.ai's model page is HTML at 317,743 bytes against fetch.py's 400,000-byte cap. One redesign, or one more section on the page, and the price parse either breaks or truncates mid-document. Mitigation: the price parser must FAIL LOUDLY when no '$' price pattern is found, never return a default; and the recorded fact must carry the quoted sentence so a later reader can see what was actually read.

The scoring instrument's validity is vendor-scoped. ByteDance state their released SyncNet is only comparable on data run through their own preprocessing, and this environment has NO ffmpeg, insightface or mediapipe (measured and documented in studio/mcp/creative.py). So the automated half of the score may be unrunnable here entirely, and the loop may close only on the human-eyeball half for some time. That must be reported as could-not-measure on the machine score, not silently skipped.

A run record is one account, one moment, one input — the probe rung exists precisely because that is weak evidence. The danger is that a single successful run gets read as 'this stack works'. Mitigation: promote_run.py mints probe tier only, and render.py should print the run COUNT next to any proved stamp, so one run never reads like a pattern.

Candidate discovery is bounded by the base's 231 ids. A model that exists in the world but not in the base cannot be proposed and — worse — cannot be seen to be missing. This section inherits Section-5-shaped coverage debt and should print, per slot, how many candidates it considered, so a slot with two candidates does not read like a survey.
Section 6 — Assembling a stack for a pro.effort:
Roughly 5 agent-sessions, plus a human in the loop for every paid run.

Session 1: attribute_families.py. This dominates the early cost and is unglamorous — it is a judgement call over 246 distinct attribute names, and the measured payoff is large (duration coverage 26 rows -> 56, price 14 -> 88) but every entry has to be justified individually.
Session 2: brief.py + check.py, including the capability-vs-applicability path and the contested path. The two negative-control tests (the 'duration' contains 'ratio' case; the unsatisfiable brief) are written here, before the assembler.
Session 3: assemble.py + render.py + silence_to_proposal.py. Mostly wiring over existing APIs; the silence ledger is the only novel logic.
Session 4: score.py + stack_runs.jsonl + promote_run.py. Blocked on whether ffmpeg and a SyncNet checkpoint can run in this environment at all — if they cannot, this session's output is the human-eyeball half plus an explicit could-not-measure on the machine score, and that is a legitimate outcome to record rather than a reason to stall.
Session 5: scripts/stack_eval.py, the frozen brief set, and breaking each of the seven gates on purpose to show it goes red.

What actually dominates the calendar is none of that: it is the wait for a human to approve and run one paid generation, and then to look at the clip. Until that happens P stays 0 and the section is, correctly, unproven.

STOP CONDITION, written before the start: if by the end of session 5 no proposal has been run and looked at — P still 0 — stop building and record what was learned about why the loop would not close (cost, approval latency, or missing scorer dependencies). Building a sixth session of reasoning layer on top of an unclosed loop is how this becomes another package of prompts nobody proved."

Section 5 — The ComfyUI ecosystem: knowi.target_state:
Checkable definition of done, in four parts.

(1) CATALOGUE. studio/knowledge/comfy_nodes.jsonl holds all 5345 registry nodes, re-swept on demand in 54 requests / 23.1 s, each row carrying id, repository, downloads, github_stars, license-as-returned, supported_comfyui_version, supported_accelerators and sweep date. This file is a machine-swept CATALOGUE and is explicitly NOT the tiered fact base; nothing in it is a claim.

(2) ADAPTER SET. Of those 5345, the 698 that pass the measured relevance rule (downloads >= 1000 AND github_stars >= 50) are the working set. 539 of the 698 (77.2%) join to a declared node-class list. Every one of the 539 carries an adapter class drawn from the eight the brief names, or the explicit label `unclassified`. Measured today on the joinable repos, the eight classes hold: LoRA loader 37, upscaler 44, ControlNet 37, video helper 25, face tools 19, IP-Adapter 12, core loader 8, AnimateDiff 5. "Done" is that these counts are reproducible and that a class with zero members is reported as zero, not omitted.

(3) THE JOIN, which is the only part that makes this useful. A node is tied to the models it drives by a four-hop path I ran end to end today, not by the registry — the registry has no model field at all. The path: registry `repository` -> extension-node-map.json (5590 repos) -> node class names -> official workflow graph node types and widget values -> model filenames -> model-list.json (562 models) `base` family -> model id in model_facts.jsonl. Proven on video_wan2_2_14B_i2v.json: 6 model filenames in the graph, 4 of them present verbatim in model-list.json, base `Wan2.2`, which the fact base already knows. Done means the join is materialised for the 539 and its miss rate is printed, not hidden.

(4) "CAN APPLY" means exactly one thing and nothing more: THE PROJECT HOLDS A RECORDED WORKFLOW GRAPH, PUBLISHED BY COMFY-ORG, WHOSE MODEL FILENAMES RESOLVE AND WHOSE minComfyUIVersion IS STATED. It does not mean the agent ran it, and it must never be recorded as if it did. 603 such graphs exist, 601 name at least one model, 168 distinct model names, and 603 of 603 carry minComfyUIVersion. That last number matters enormously because the registry's own supported_comfyui_version is empty for 5129 of 5345 nodes (95.96%) — the templates, not the registry, are where version compatibility actually lives. To claim more than "recorded and resolvable" — to claim the recipe RUNS — would require a ComfyUI instance the agent does not have; that is a paid/hosted measurement and goes through scripts/measurement.py as a proposal, exactly like a paid generation.

build.does: The licence gate, and it is far more work than the brief's framing implies. THE REGISTRY LICENCE FIELD DOES NOT ANSWER THE LICENCE QUESTION — measured over all 5345: 2981 (55.8%) are the bare pointer {"file": "LICENSE"} with no licence named, 1334 (25.0%) are absent or {}, leaving ~1030 (19.3%) with any text at all, and that text is free-form rather than SPDX — {"text": "MIT"} 401, {"text": "MIT License"} 123, {"text": "LICENSE"} 78, {"text": "Apache-2.0"} 76, {"text": "GNU General Public License v3"} 42, {"text": "MIT license"} 35, plus bare literals. So 80.7% of nodes cannot be licence-cleared from the registry. This script therefore fetches the actual LICENSE file from raw.githubusercontent.com per shortlisted node (open host, ~698 fetches, checkpointed and resumable), normalises to SPDX, and emits pass / fail / could-not-measure per node. Anything matching non-commercial, research-only, OpenRAIL or CC-BY-NC is flagged BEFORE integration and never silently. Prints `checked N, restrictive M, could-not-determine K` — three numbers, never a bare boolean.

build.why_not_simpler: Because the simple version is a lie with a green tick. Trusting the registry field would clear 2981 nodes whose licence is literally the string 'LICENSE'. build.does: Turn a (model, adapter class) request into a RECORDED RECIPE and be honest about its status. Returns: the template name and its raw.githubusercontent URL, its minComfyUIVersion, its openSource flag, the model filenames it needs, which of those resolve in model-list.json with a download URL and which do not, and the node packages that must be installed with their licence verdicts. Status is one of `recorded-and-resolvable` (every filename resolves, version stated, licences clear), `recorded-with-gaps` (names the exact missing filenames — for video_wan2_2_14B_i2v that is the two lightx2v LoRAs), or `no-recipe`. It NEVER returns `runs`. Claiming that requires a ComfyUI instance, which the agent does not have and must not pretend to; that is a hosted measurement filed through studio/mcp/proposal.py and approved by a human with scripts/measurement.py, exactly as a paid generation is.

Everything short of an execution is a document, and calling a document an execution is how this section would quietly become the least trustworthy thing in the repository. The three-way status is what keeps the 325 closed-source API templates from being handed to a user as local capability.

build.does: The ONLY writer from this section into studio/knowledge/model_facts.jsonl, and it does not write unattended. It emits a harvest file of candidate claims — attribute names like comfy_adapter_available, comfy_workflow_template, comfy_min_comfyui_version — each with a source_url and a QUOTED evidence string lifted verbatim from the fetched artefact (the template's own models[] entry, the model-list row, the LICENSE text). WHAT STOPS A BLOG ENTERING AS VENDOR: nothing in this pipeline states a rung. api.comfy.org and raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/ are added to studio/selfrag/source_hosts.py as PORTAL — Comfy-Org runs the system, so its statements are about a running system, but it is not the vendor of Wan or FLUX and must never tier as one. A script that appends 5345 machine-swept rows to it destroys exactly that property in one commit, and no later cleanup restores it — which is why the catalogue lives in its own file and only the joined, evidence-quoted minority is ever proposed for promotion. Section 5 — The ComfyUI ecosystem: knowi.effort:
Roughly 5 to 6 agent-sessions, and the shape of the cost is lopsided — the collection is nearly free and the honesty is where the time goes.

What is NOT in this estimate, and should not be smuggled in: executing a single workflow. There is no ComfyUI instance here. findings.problem: studio/harvest/deployment_ids.py, as specified, DELETES the contradiction the whole section exists to preserve. findings.fix: Do not ship deployment_ids.py before FactStore knows about qualified ids. Whichever is chosen, add a pinned regression asserting the contested count over the live base does not fall as a side effect of the migration — literal expected values (Т2), and run it before and after (И2).

findings.problem: `<model>@<host>` is the wrong granularity, measured. I opened https://fal.ai/api/models?keywords=veo (200, 16,106 bytes): fal alone publishes 13 endpoints under modelFamily 'Veo 3.1' — fal-ai/veo3.1, /fast, /lite, /image-to-video, /first-last-frame-to-video, /reference-to-video, /extend-video and combinations — with DIFFERENT ceilings and prices per endpoint ('$0.20 without audio ... at 4k $0.40' for veo3.1, '$0.05 for 720p with audio ... findings.fix: Qualify with the deployment endpoint id, not the host: `veo-3.1@fal.ai/veo3.1/lite`. The endpoint id is present verbatim in both the inventory (`items[].id`) and the OpenAPI (`x-fal-metadata.endpointId`), so it needs no invention. findings.problem: scripts/check/spec_staleness.py writes into the fact base with no human between: 'A `changed` result files a withdrawal-plus-new-claim pair', reusing studio/mcp/advice.py record/withdraw — both of which append directly to studio/knowledge/model_facts.jsonl (advice.py:446 record, :658 withdraw). findings.fix: Make spec_staleness.py read-only. It emits a rechecks file (studio/knowledge/harvests/<date>_rechecks.jsonl) with unchanged/changed/could-not-recheck per claim and exits non-zero on `changed`; the withdrawal-plus-new-claim pair is written only by scripts/ingest_harvest.py under a human run, exactly like every other write. Add a negative control that the check leaves model_facts.jsonl byte-identical (assert the file hash before and after).

findings.problem: The three commands the target state is 'checkable by' cannot exist as written. scripts/check is not a directory — it is an executable bash file, 9,391 bytes, whose header reads 'Single source of truth for all checks: CI runs this same script'. So `python scripts/check/spec_vocab.py`, `python scripts/check/deployment_ids.py` and scripts/check/spec_staleness.py collide with an existing file, and the plan bypasses the repo's one CI entry point rather than extending it (ground 6: the runner already exists).

findings.problem: The canonical vocabulary is a list of NAMES, but the contradiction machinery compares VALUES by exact string equality (facts.py:367, `by_value[fact.value]`). Renaming Runway's `max_resolution`='1920:1080 (1080p max, no 4K)' and fal's `resolution_enum`='720p, 1080p, 4k' onto one attribute makes them collide as three different strings; it does not make them comparable. Worse, the vocabulary introduces list-shaped attributes (`resolution_enum`, `aspect_ratio_enum`, `duration_enum_seconds`) and never mentions MULTI_VALUED (facts.py:184). Both branches are bad and neither is chosen: inside MULTI_VALUED, a genuine 4k-vs-no-4k disagreement prints as '3 value(s) recorded', outcome pass — a gate that cannot go red; outside it, '720p, 1080p, 4K' vs '720p,1080p,4k' prints as contested — a gate that is red on cosmetics.
findings.fix: Ship a value normalizer alongside the name table in studio/knowledge/spec_vocabulary.py: per canonical attribute, a declared value shape (sorted token set for enums, integer pixel-height for ceilings, seconds for durations) applied at ingest, with the verbatim quote kept untouched in `evidence`. State explicitly which of the canonical names go into MULTI_VALUED and why, and make the decision testable: a fixture where fal says 4k and Runway does not must report `fail`, and a fixture where two sources state the same enum in different order must report `pass`.

findings.problem: The flagship justification for spec_vocabulary.py is misattributed. findings.fix: Re-anchor the vocabulary's why_not_simpler on the 246 names and the 8/12/20 spellings (all reproduced), which justify it on their own, and move the Veo 3.1 example to variant_binding.py / merge_model_ids.py where it belongs. findings.problem: Scope promises a set that is never defined. The target state says 'every model in the coverable slice (defined below)' and no definition appears below — no model list, no N, no inventory step, no fetch budget. Every channel in the section is one-model-per-call or one-endpoint-per-call, and the volume of the inventory is left as an adjective ('at scale' in the title, 'the endpoint inventory comes from fal.ai/api/models?keywords=...' with no count). findings.problem: Four of the twelve canonical attributes have no opened channel, while the section title promises all of them. rate_limit_rpm: the one probed source is a JS shell, 0 rows recovered (the section says so). eol_date: no feed probed, 1 lifecycle row in the base (I confirmed: exactly 1). price_per_second_usd: no price channel appears in the `measured` list at all — the only price mention is Kokoro's card citing artificialanalysis.ai, a refused host. context_window_tokens: not addressed by a single probed channel and not even mentioned in risks; the two candidate sources (openai-openapi/openapi.yaml, platform.openai.com) are truncated and JS-shelled respectively.

findings.problem: Gate 4's fixture asserts 'exactly 3 output-resolution rows, exactly one of which carries 4K' against a document the section itself measured as TRUNCATED (399,955 bytes read of a page exceeding the 400,000-byte cap, 'tail cuts mid-way through the model-id mapping table'). If a count is asserted, assert it as 'at least 3 in the readable prefix' and record it as РАСЧЁТ on a truncated read (И4), with the total left as could-not-measure until the page is readable whole.

Introduced before the backfill it is red on day one, which is how a gate gets commented out; the effort section budgets the backfill but the plan gives no ordering constraint linking the two.

Section 1 — The model range: how the bas.section: Section 1 — The model range: how the base goes from 231 ids to covering the field, and where the field honestly ends
Section 1 — The model range: how the bas.what_it_gets_right: The measurement is real and it reproduces. I re-fetched huggingface.co/api/models?pipeline_tag=text-to-video&sort=likes&limit=100 with skip=0 and skip=100 through studio/mcp/fetch.py and got exactly 162 repos at likes>=25, 45 derivatives, 117 kept — the section's three headline numbers, independently. ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models answered 200 for me too, despite fetch.py's own docstring listing that host as closed, which is the path-not-host rule the module documents working in the section's favour. skip=4000 answered 400 with the deprecation message, as claimed. Three structural choices are correct and worth keeping: discovery writes candidates_<date>.jsonl and never facts (scripts/discover_models.py), the import-boundary test that makes a future --auto flag show up in a diff, and reading the litellm file off an anonymous git clone rather than looking for an HTTP mirror of a host that truncates. The 401-not-404 negative control for retirement is a genuine negative control, and the closed-LLM single-source weakness is stated rather than dressed up.

findings.problem: The derivative rule names tag strings that do not exist. HF emits base_model:adapter:<repo>, base_model:quantized:<repo>, base_model:merge:<repo> — the base model id is a third segment. studio/discovery/derivative.py is specified as membership in the set {base_model:adapter, base_model:quantized, base_model:merge}. MEASURED by me today on the text-to-video likes>=25 pool (162 rows): exact membership match drops 0 of 162; prefix match drops 45 and leaves the section's own 117. Sample tags read verbatim: 'base_model:quantized:Lightricks/LTX-2.3', 'base_model:adapter:Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3'. Implemented as written, the rule that the section calls 'mechanical rather than a guess' is a no-op that passes every LoRA and GGUF repack through as a model.
findings.fix: State the rule as a prefix/segment match on the tag ('base_model' + ':' + kind + ':' + base_id, kind in {adapter, quantized, merge}), and put the literal tag string 'base_model:quantized:Lightricks/LTX-2.3' into the frozen fixture in gate 2 so the expected-value literal encodes the real format (T2). The published selection rule in the README must quote the real tag shape, not the abbreviated one.

findings.problem: The coverage gate's only failure mode is a number going down. scripts/check/coverage.py asserts a FLOOR of >=117 kept for text-to-video. Combined with finding 1 this is not hypothetical: the broken exact-match rule keeps all 162, which is above the floor, so the gate reports green while the derivative rule is inert. Both declared negative controls (limit=1000 truncation; a nonexistent pipeline_tag) test only undercounting and zero-fetch. Nothing in the gate can go red for over-keeping.
findings.fix: Assert the pair, not the floor: kept >= 117 AND dropped >= 45 AND kept + dropped + undecidable == fetched, each an ИЗМЕРЕНО constant dated 2026-08-28. Add a third negative control that removes the ':' segment handling from the tag matcher — dropped falls to 0 and the gate must go red on the dropped-count assertion.

findings.problem: Scope promises six slices but is sized for one. The target state says the base holds a read, tiered fact for EVERY repo passing the rule in six slices; every count, the effort estimate and the only coverage floor cover text-to-video alone. MEASURED by me today at likes>=25: image-to-video ~182 (100 at skip=0, 82 at skip=100), text-to-speech ~274 (100/100/74 across three pages, min likes 22 at skip=200), text-to-image ~1251 (still 100/100 above 25 at skip=1000, min likes 23 at skip=1200), text-generation far past that — at skip=1000 the page still runs 148 down to 134 likes. That is well over 2000 candidates, each needing a human-approved, quoted promotion, against an estimate of 6-8 sessions.
findings.fix: Either restate DONE as a per-slice slice-of-a-slice with its own measured floor and its own ВЫБРАНО likes constant (the section already concedes 25 is wrong for TTS), or keep likes>=25 only for the two video slices and publish the measured candidate count for all six before committing to 'every repo'. State a per-week promotion rate and the total, so the gap between discovered and promoted is a printed number (Е3) rather than a coverage percentage that looks healthy.

findings.problem: Two slices are already past the working skip window, so the paging dependency is not future risk but a present blocker. MEASURED today: text-generation skip=4000 -> 400 'The `skip` query parameter is deprecated...Use the `links` response header instead', and skip=5900 -> 400. text-to-image and text-generation candidate sets are both deeper than the depth skip still serves. The Link-header change to fetch.py is listed as a footnote that must be handed to another writer under Ц2 — meaning the entire discovery build is gated on a handoff that the plan sequences last.
findings.fix: Move the fetch.py header change to step one with its own acceptance test (a fetch returning the Link header for a paged HF call), and make it a stated precondition: until it lands, discovery covers only text-to-video and image-to-video, and the other four slices report could-not-measure rather than a truncated count.

findings.problem: Gate 4's tier assertion contradicts studio/selfrag/source_hosts.py and would go red on correct existing rows. The gate asserts every fact whose source_url host is huggingface.co carries tier portal or blog. classify() at source_hosts.py:301 is model-aware: it checks vendor_sources_for(model) first, and the table maps 'huggingface.co/tencent/', 'huggingface.co/Wan-AI/', 'huggingface.co/Qwen/', 'huggingface.co/stabilityai/', 'huggingface.co/THUDM/' and others as VENDOR for their own models. A HunyuanVideo card read off huggingface.co/tencent/ is vendor tier today, by design.
findings.fix: Assert the invariant that actually matters: the recorded tier must equal classify(model, url, ...) for every row, and no code path outside advice.record may set a tier literal. Drop the 'huggingface.co is always portal' clause — the section's own prose for promote_candidates.py already states the correct rule ('unless source_hosts.py already knows tencent as that model's vendor'); only the gate contradicts it.

findings.problem: scripts/check/coverage.py and scripts/check/retirement.py cannot be created as specified: scripts/check is an executable bash file (9391 bytes, 'Bourne-Again shell script'), the single CI entry point that runs ruff/mypy/unittest. Creating that directory means deleting or renaming the file every check in this repo is invoked through, and it belongs to another writer (Ц2).
findings.fix: Put them at scripts/check_coverage.py and scripts/check_retirement.py, and add two lines invoking them to the existing scripts/check script via a handoff to its writer — which is also what makes them run in CI (Ц7) rather than only on request.

findings.problem: The derivative module is justified with video-slice evidence and presented as the field-wide rule. MEASURED today with prefix matching on the top 100 by likes: text-to-video 45 derivatives in the 162-row candidate set, but text-to-speech only 2 of 100 and text-to-image 16 of 100. On TTS the rule is close to inert, so the fixture set and the floor mutations in gate 2 prove nothing about the slice where the floor is most doubtful.
findings.fix: Measure the drop rate per slice before shipping, record each as a separate ИЗМЕРЕНО constant with its date, and take gate 2's 30 frozen rows from at least three slices rather than from text-to-video alone (Т3 applies across slices, not just across the likes range).

Section 3 — Applicability in the communi.section: Section 3 — Applicability in the community: what people actually get out of these models
Section 3 — Applicability in the communi.what_it_gets_right: The channels are real and I reproduced them rather than taking the word for it. I re-fetched https://huggingface.co/api/models/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/discussions?type=discussion&status=open&p=0 through mcp__lipsync-studio__fetch_url: 200, 29368 bytes, "count":45, "start":0, "numClosedDiscussions":13, exactly 45 thread objects in the body, each carrying num, title, numComments, createdAt, author, numReactionUsers and repoOwner.isParticipating — and the quoted titles are there verbatim ("custom audio lipsync for ltx 2.5 just doesnt work", "The character consistency in i2v is a disaster.", "LTX 2.5 Just Changed Local AI Video Forever!" and "LTX 2.5 on RTX 3060..." both by LabMike3D, i.e. the astroturf risk is measured, not imagined). No volume figure in this section is an adjective. The Reddit finding checks out against the repository: studio/selfrag/source_hosts.py:237-238 does list reddit.com/r/comfyui/ and old.reddit.com/r/comfyui/ in PORTAL_SOURCES, and the module's own docstring already says it is not a reachability map. Nothing in the plan depends on a host the egress policy refuses, nothing writes model_facts.jsonl unattended (the staging-file-plus-human-ingest boundary is the right shape and it is the existing one), and separating volume from evidence by SCHEMA — no `evidence` field, so scripts/ingest_harvest.py:_malformed cannot accept it — is a structurally sound idea rather than a convention. The downloads 745 vs downloadsAllTime 53419 window trap is a genuine measurement with a real consequence. The stop condition (Ц9) is written and is falsifiable.

findings.problem: The section's load-bearing claim — "the tier is decided by the URL" — produces `vendor` for community complaints, and gate 2's negative control asserts a premise that is false in today's repository. I ran it: `source_hosts.classify('ltx-2.5', 'https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/discussions/44', ...)` returns **vendor**, because studio/selfrag/source_hosts.py:136 already has "ltx": ("huggingface.co/Lightricks/",) in VENDOR_SOURCES and _matches is a path-prefix test. The same thread via the API path returns `portal` only because "/api/models/Lightricks/..." does not start with "Lightricks/". So the rung of a practitioner's "the character consistency in i2v is a disaster" depends on which of two URLs for the same document the collector happens to store — and the human-readable one, the one a reviewer would actually open to check the quote, is the one that classifies as the vendor's own statement. Gate 2's second control ("still `portal` until a human adds huggingface.co/Lightricks/ to VENDOR_SOURCES") is written against a table entry that has been there since 2026-08-27, and would pass today for the wrong reason.
findings.fix: Decide this before writing the collector, and gate it. Either (a) add a rule to source_hosts that a /discussions/ path segment is community text and never the vendor's rung — the same shape as the existing BLOG_PATH_SEGMENTS carve-out, which already demotes a portal's /blog/ page — or (b) state explicitly that community rows carry the api.* URL and add a gate asserting that the canonical huggingface.co/<org>/<repo>/discussions/<n> URL classifies portal, not vendor, for a model whose vendor org is that org. Test it on ltx (vendor org listed) and on a model whose org is NOT in VENDOR_SOURCES, so the gate distinguishes the two. Fix the negative control to remove huggingface.co/Lightricks/ from VENDOR_SOURCES and assert the classification CHANGES — right now it asserts an addition that already exists.

findings.problem: Gate 1 asserts a refusal message that the code does not emit, and a negative control that cannot go green — so its T1 mutation proves nothing. scripts/ingest_harvest.py:_malformed loops over (model, attribute, value, source_url, tier, evidence) and returns "empty <field>" BEFORE reaching the MIN_EVIDENCE_CHARS check at :176. The adoption row the gate feeds it — {model, metric, value, window, source_url} — has no `attribute`, no `tier`, no `evidence` and no `read_directly`, so it is refused with "empty attribute", never "evidence too short to be a quotation". The negative control ("the same row with a real 40-character quote added is ACCEPTED") is therefore impossible: it is still missing attribute, tier and read_directly. Consequently mutating MIN_EVIDENCE_CHARS to 0 does not turn the refusing half green and 10000 does not turn the accepting half red — the constant is not what this test is watching, which is exactly the rot the negative control was supposed to prevent.
findings.fix: Split it into two gates with honest assertions. (1) The schema gate: assert the adoption row is refused and assert on the actual reason string produced by _malformed's required-field loop; that gate's negative control is a row with every required field present. (2) The quotation gate: a row that is complete in every other respect and differs ONLY in evidence length — 11 chars refused, 40 chars accepted. That second pair is the one that survives mutating MIN_EVIDENCE_CHARS in both directions, and only it should claim T1.

findings.problem: Gate 3's base-level assertion cannot go red, because it describes agreement, not a contest. FactStore.contested() (studio/selfrag/facts.py:554) reports a (model, attribute) only when claims() returns FAIL, i.e. when sources DISAGREE on the value. A fixture of "10 identical-value portal rows" is ten sources agreeing; the attribute will not be contested at all, so "assert the attribute is still reported CONTESTED" fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the consensus trap the gate exists to catch. The real risk being described — count outweighing a dissenting source — is never exercised.
findings.fix: Build the fixture as one dissenting row (say a vendor or probe row with value B) plus ten portal rows carrying value A, and assert the attribute is STILL reported contested and that claims() names both values with their tiers — majority did not resolve it. Negative control: drop to one row of each and assert it is still contested (so the gate is not measuring row count), and remove the dissenting row and assert it is NOT contested (so the gate can go green legitimately).

findings.problem: The slice is narrower than the target state admits, and the narrowing is invisible in the numbers quoted. Every channel URL pins status=open. The listing I fetched reports "numClosedDiscussions": 13 alongside "count": 45 — 22% of the threads on this repo are excluded by a query parameter mentioned nowhere in the target state or the risks. Closed threads are disproportionately the resolved ones: the vendor answered, a working configuration was found, the bug was fixed in a release. That is precisely the "what people actually get out of model X" material this section promises, and the "45 threads are the calibration set" claim is really a 45-of-58 slice chosen by a default.
findings.fix: Either collect status=all and record `thread_status` on every row (a closed thread's resolution is stronger evidence than an open complaint, not weaker), or state in the target state that the section covers OPEN threads only, give the measured 45/13 split as the reason, and print closed-thread counts per model in the run summary so the excluded volume is visible rather than assumed away.

findings.problem: The stated cost control is a no-op on the measured data. hf_discussions.thread_refs is specified to skip a thread with 0 comments without a request, "exactly the way civitai.version_refs uses hasPositivePrompt". Of the 45 threads I read, the minimum numComments is 1 and the median is around 3 — nothing would be skipped. The analogy does not hold either: hasPositivePrompt prunes a majority of Civitai versions, whereas numComments counts REPLIES, and the report with the settings in it is frequently the opening post (e.g. thread 59, "A2Vid two-stage (LTX-2.5): stage 2 distilled refine corrupts non-keyframe latents", numComments 1). A filter on replies would drop good single-post bug reports while saving nothing.
findings.fix: Drop the numComments filter or invert it into a priority order rather than a skip, and state the real budget honestly: 1 listing request plus up to N thread requests per model, with N an explicit page/thread budget as a stop condition. If a cheap pre-filter is wanted, the measured discriminator is the title plus numReactionUsers, not numComments — and either way, print how many threads were opened versus available.

findings.problem: Gate 5 (the live-channel canary) is specified as "excluded from the offline suite and run deliberately", with no runner, no cadence and no owner. Its only failure mode is that nobody runs it — which is the failure mode it was written to prevent for the channels themselves. Ц7: a thing that must always happen is a hook, a test or CI, not a sentence.
findings.fix: Give it a schedule and a place: a network-marked target invoked by a named CI job on a stated cadence (weekly is enough for a shape change), whose could-not-measure result is reported as could-not-measure with the HTTP status and does NOT fail the build, but DOES fail loudly and visibly. Say who reads that output. Keep the negative controls — they are well chosen.

findings.problem: The adoption ledger's committed/ignored status is contradictory and undone. Gate 6 asserts "adoption ledgers are still gitignored", but .gitignore today contains no such line (it ignores studio/knowledge/civitai_prompts.jsonl and the gallery wording, nothing about adoption_*.jsonl), and the build item lists studio/knowledge/adoption_<date>.jsonl as a knowledge artefact without saying it is private. A gate asserting a .gitignore line that does not exist starts red on day one, which is better than silent — but the underlying decision is unmade: adoption numbers are public counters read from public APIs, so it is not obvious they need to be private at all, and if they are ignored the ledger cannot be reviewed or diffed.
findings.fix: Make the call explicitly and say why: HF/Civitai/Comfy counters are facts about a page, not third-party creative text, so the argument for ignoring them is weaker than for civitai_prompts.jsonl. If they are to be committed, remove that clause from gate 6; if ignored, add the .gitignore line in the same session as the gate.

findings.problem: The dedupe rule is invented without naming the near-duplicate logic already in the repository. studio/selfrag/evidence.py (craft_phrases) already carries a near-duplicate rule with a stated threshold — "two clauses sharing more than half their words say the same thing twice" — and it is exercised by studio/selfrag/tests/test_evidence.py:102 and studio/tests/test_knowledge.py:772. The plan's shingle threshold would be a second, differently-tuned notion of "same text" in the same codebase (Е1).
findings.fix: Name it in `reuses` and say why a second rule is needed — the honest answer is probably that evidence.py's rule operates on short prompt clauses and this one on multi-paragraph posts, which is a real difference. If a new threshold is introduced, mark its origin per И4 (ВЫБРАНО by whom, from what) and mutate it in both directions as gate 3 already promises.

Section 4 — Features, quirks, defects an.section: Section 4 — Features, quirks, defects and glitches
Section 4 — Features, quirks, defects an.what_it_gets_right: The channel work is real and I reproduced it: https://huggingface.co/api/models?pipeline_tag=text-to-video&sort=likes&direction=-1&limit=25 answered 200 with the documented fields, and https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Wan2.2-Lightning/raw/main/README.md answered 200 at 19,309 bytes. GitHub is handled correctly — declared shut by four measured routes, no mirror, and gate 6 greps for the reflex, which is the right shape. The 60-80 vendor-repo figure is explicitly labelled an estimate rather than dressed up as a count. The defect_grammar accept/refuse boundary is drawn through real sentences from the same page (LTX-Video's own '## Limitations' as the negative control) rather than invented ones, and both mutation directions are named. The floor gate is honestly monotone, so it has exactly one failure mode and that mode is real loss. The scope paragraph refuses to say 'all models'. Reuse is genuine: fetch.py as the one door, ingest_harvest.py as the only writer, civitai.py as the shape for the per-model collector — I found no module in the repo that already does sentence-level defect grammar (studio/selfrag/evidence.py is prompt-craft phrases, not claims).

findings.problem: FactStore.reproduction() will manufacture 'reproduced by N independent hosts' out of copy-paste, and I measured the exact case using this section's own ACCEPT fixture. https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Wan2.2-Lightning/raw/main/README.md (fetched today, 200, 19,309 bytes) contains verbatim: 'If you encounter OOM (Out-of-Memory) issues, you can use the `--offload_model True`, `--convert_model_dtype` and `--t5_cpu` options to reduce GPU memory usage.' — the same sentence the blueprint quotes from raw.githubusercontent.com/Wan-Video/Wan2.2. lightx2v is a third party that copied Wan's README; two distinct hosts under source_hosts.host_of, zero independent reproduction. The failure is two-sided: because studio/selfrag/facts.py:259 claim_key compares value by exact strip(), the two texts differ by the trailing clause and would NOT match, so with strict matching the label almost never fires on real prose, and any fuzzy relaxation fires precisely on inherited README text. Gate 4 cannot catch either direction because its fixture is three CONSTRUCTED rows.
findings.fix: Count independent PROVENANCE, not hosts: exclude any source whose HF card declares a base_model/adapter relation to another model in the slice (the field is in the /api/models rows already being fetched — e.g. lightx2v/Wan2.2-Lightning lists base_model Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B), and require a normalised-text non-identity check so a byte-copy of another card's sentence counts once. Rebuild gate 4's fixture from these two REAL urls (Wan-Video README vs lightx2v card, same sentence) and assert it reports 'reported by 1 source'; keep the constructed rows only for the same-host-twice case.

findings.problem: The headline promise — that (b) 'no defect stated by any source we could read, with the count of sources read' prints differently from (c) 'could not read this model's sources, with the HTTP statuses' — has nothing durable behind it. model_advice reads the fact base; a model that was fetched and stated no defect produces no row and is byte-identical, at advise() time, to a model nobody ever fetched. The only place the read/unread distinction exists in the build is harvest_defects.py's three per-RUN counters (read N / stated M / could-not-read K), which are aggregate, not per model, and which advise() cannot see. So the 10 gated 401 models and the 23/47 video cards with no defect signal will all render as (b) or all as (c) depending on which default advise() picks — the two-outcome collapse the section says it exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Add a per-model coverage record the harvest writes and advise reads: studio/knowledge/defect_coverage_<date>.jsonl with {model, urls_tried, http_status per url, sentences_examined, defects_stated, read_on}. Name it in the build list, name which module reads it in advise output, and add the assertion to gate 2 that a model present in coverage with status 401 renders (c) while a model with status 200 and defects_stated=0 renders (b) — with the two strings asserted as literals.

findings.problem: Channel 1 declares tier 'vendor' for huggingface.co/{owner}/{model}/raw/main/README.md, but for most of the slice that host is portal, and ingest will refuse the row rather than downgrade it. MEASURED just now by running studio.selfrag.source_hosts.classify over the 25 top-liked text-to-video ids returned by the API: 9 classify vendor (hunyuanvideo, wan2.*, mochi-1-preview, cogvideox-*), 16 classify portal (sulphur-2-base, animatediff-lightning, minimax-h3-turbo-lora, pyramid-flow-sd3, longcat-video, stepvideo-t2v, zeroscope_v2_576w, hotshot-xl, animatelcm, ...). Extrapolated to the 125 unknown models this is roughly a hundred VENDOR_SOURCES entries of per-family judgement that the plan never budgets, and advice.record refuses every mismatched row with 'tier does not match the URL'.
findings.fix: Do not assert a tier in the channel table. Have harvest_defects.py call source_hosts.classify for each card and write the tier the URL earns, and add a fourth printed counter, 'cards whose own org is not declared vendor: N', with the list of orgs, so each sweep produces the source_hosts.py edit list the way the 2026-08-27 harvest's 44 refusals did. State the measured 9/25 in the channel entry so the next reader knows the shape of the work.

findings.problem: 'Every Hugging Face model with >=100 likes' is not a slice of models, it is a slice of repositories, and a large part of it is third-party derivatives whose defect sentences are about somebody else's weights. In the top 25 by likes for text-to-video alone, at least eight are LoRAs, distillations, quantizations or merges: SulphurAI/Sulphur-2-base (base_model Lightricks/LTX-2.3), larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora, drbaph/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora-ComfyUI, lightx2v/Wan2.2-Lightning, vrgamedevgirl84/Wan14BT2VFusioniX, Alissonerdx/LTX-Best-Face-ID, SexGod1979/PinkCherry_MiniMax-H3, ByteDance/AnimateDiff-Lightning. Coverage counted over this slice inflates: a derivative card counts as a covered model while telling you nothing new about the model anyone will actually be advised on.
findings.fix: Split the slice explicitly and report the halves separately: BASE models (no base_model/adapter/quantized tag in the API row) and DERIVATIVES. Put only the base half into the stop condition's >=60% target, and say in target_state which half the 125 unknown models fall into — that count should be re-derived per tag, not carried as one number.

findings.problem: Gate 2 pins a number that comes from a live, moving list: 'sweeping the top-100 list must report could-not-read = 10'. The top-25-by-likes ranking changes weekly — today's text-to-video page already contains models created in 2026-08 (larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora, drbaph/..., created 2026-08-05/06). As written the gate either goes to the network (Т4: a test that reds from someone else's outage and greens from a cache) or runs against an unspecified fixture. The section never says which.
findings.fix: Freeze the sweep input as a repo fixture: the 100 {id, url} rows and the recorded per-url HTTP status from this run, checked in beside the test, with the live sweep a separate reported command whose output goes in the report. Assert the counters against the frozen fixture only, and let the fixture's date be part of its filename so its staleness is visible.

findings.problem: scripts/ingest_harvest.py stamps a hardcoded date: READ_ON = '2026-08-27' (line 73) is used for stated_on AND written into every row's note as 'HARVESTED 2026-08-27 ... (stated_on is the day it was READ)'. A harvest_defects_<date>.jsonl ingested in a later session gets a false read date on every defect row, and stale_model_facts then ages them from the wrong day. DEFAULT_HARVEST (line 64) is likewise pinned to harvest_2026-08-27.jsonl.
findings.fix: Derive READ_ON from the harvest file — a per-row read_on field, falling back to the date parsed out of the filename — and fail loudly when neither is present. This is a one-file change in the module the section already depends on, and it belongs in the build list rather than being discovered on the second harvest.

findings.problem: The build entry for harvest_defects.py says it 'never states a tier of vendor/portal/blog', but scripts/ingest_harvest.py:167-171 refuses any row with an empty tier field as malformed before advice.record ever sees it, and a malformed row makes main() return 1. Taken literally, every row of the first defect harvest is counted 'негодных' and the ingest fails.
findings.fix: Reword to what is actually true and safe: the harvester never CHOOSES a rung by judgement, it writes the rung source_hosts.classify returns for that URL, and record() re-checks it. Same effect, and it passes _malformed.

findings.problem: 'Nothing this section builds writes to model_facts.jsonl ... only scripts/ingest_harvest.py stamps them' reads as a human gate, but ingest_harvest.py is a non-interactive script an agent can run in the same session as the harvest; the repo's human-approval rule covers paid generation (proposal.py/measurement.py), not fact writes. At 90 cards a sweep this is the first place in the plan where a bad grammar change reaches the base unattended.
findings.fix: Write the two-step into the section: a defect harvest is ingested with --dry-run first, the refusal counts and the top refusal reasons go into the report verbatim, and the non-dry run is a separate command. That is the workflow the script's own docstring already prescribes; saying so makes the omission gradable.

Section 6 — Assembling a stack for a pro.section: Section 6 — Assembling a stack for a product task: the reasoning layer, and the loop that proves it
Section 6 — Assembling a stack for a pro.what_it_gets_right: Reproduced its two most load-bearing channel claims (comfy search ignored; the syncnet/EEG negative control) and confirmed every local API it names exists; the capability-vs-applicability split as a code path, the probe-only promotion door, the stated scope slice, and the admission that P starts at 0 are the parts worth keeping unchanged.

findings.problem: The per-slot candidate universe is asserted but nothing produces it. assemble.py says it "walks the slots (plate ingest, presenter, lip-sync, audio, join)" over "the 231-id fact base as the candidate universe", reusing FactStore.near() for candidate discovery. near() is a spelling-neighbour finder, not a capability index — its docstring says "ids in the base that share a prefix", and I ran it: near('latentsync') -> ['latentsync-1.0','latentsync-1.5']; near('elevenlabs-tts') -> eight elevenlabs-* ids including scribe-v2 (speech-to-text) and music. And fact rows carry no capability field at all — the keys are exactly ['attribute','model','note','read_directly','source_url','stated_on','tier','value']. So 'which ids are lip-sync candidates' is underivable from the base, and a slot will be populated by whatever the author happened to type — the exact unfalsifiable step the quoted_brief_text field was invented to prevent, one level up.
findings.fix: Add an explicit slot-membership table in the same shape as source_hosts.py/attribute_families.py (id -> slot(s), one line per id with a one-line why), or state plainly that candidate sets are hand-listed per brief and printed verbatim in the proposal. Either way stack_eval.py must print candidates-considered per slot and the count of base ids with no slot entry, so an unslotted id is counted, never dropped.

findings.problem: The section fixes attribute-name fragmentation and ignores model-id fragmentation, which is live in the same file and bites the same way. Measured now over model_facts.jsonl: eleven-v3 14 rows AND eleven_v3 14 AND elevenlabs-eleven-v3 8; eleven-flash-v2-5 8 vs eleven_flash_v2_5 5 vs eleven-flash-v2.5 2; and the section's own worked model is split latentsync 10 / latentsync-1.5 2 / latentsync-1.0 2. That is why model_advice('latentsync') reported 11 rows — it did not see the versioned rows, and the vendor VRAM line the section quotes (8 GB for 1.5, 18 GB for 1.6) is version-scoped. check() keyed on one spelling therefore reads a subset of the evidence and reports SILENCE the base does not have — the identical defect the why_not_simpler for attribute_families.py argues is fatal. scripts/merge_model_ids.py documents this class and ships a --check mode, but no gate runs it.
findings.fix: Either canonicalise the model id inside check() through merge_model_ids' canonical map, or add an id-family table alongside attribute_families.py. Add `python scripts/merge_model_ids.py --check` to stack_eval.py's gates and print the count of unmerged spellings next to the unfamilied-attribute count.

findings.problem: Gate 1's first negative control cannot go red as written. "Delete the 15 aspect_ratio rows, re-run — every brief containing 'vertical' must flip from pass to could-not-measure" only detects anything if some such brief passes at baseline. But target_state (c) forbids `pass` whenever silence is non-zero, and the section's own measurement says 13 of 244 ids have any aspect-ratio row (5%). So the baseline for a 'vertical' brief is almost certainly already could-not-measure, the deletion changes nothing observable, and a checker that never reads aspect_ratio at all passes this control.
findings.fix: Require the frozen brief set to contain at least one brief that PASSES at baseline against pinned fixture facts (a winner that does hold an aspect_ratio row), and assert the exact transition on that brief plus the reason string naming aspect_ratio. If no brief passes at baseline, the gate must report could-not-measure — not pass — and say so.

findings.problem: Done = `proved P > 0` depends on a machine score that cannot be produced in this environment, and the package never resolves the contradiction. Gate 5 counts P only for run records carrying all three score fields (machine score, negative-control score, human note) and score.py "returns all three or nothing"; risk 5 concedes the machine half may be unrunnable. Measured here: `python3 -c "import torch"` and `import cv2` both ModuleNotFoundError, no ffmpeg/ffprobe on PATH, and studio/mcp/creative.py's own header states ffmpeg, insightface and mediapipe are NOT present. So P is 0 by construction for a reason unrelated to whether anyone ran a clip — the section's single done-criterion is unreachable, and the pressure will be to quietly redefine P.
findings.fix: Split the counter before building: `proved-by-instrument P1` (machine score + offset control + note) and `proved-by-eye P2` (artefact + human note, machine score recorded explicitly as could-not-measure with the missing dependency named). Make the dependency question a session-1 cheap check (rule P2), not a session-4 discovery, and state which of P1/P2 the done gate requires.

findings.problem: The call into proposal.py as specified would be refused. Both target_state (d) and silence_to_proposal.py list the fields as gap / test / cost_usd / cost_basis / decides — but propose() also requires `task` (keyword-only, MIN_TASK_CHARS enforced) and returns outcome fail, "not filed: task is empty" without it. Two further behaviours the design assumes away: propose() dedupes on sha256(model|attribute|normalised test), so "queue length is the honest measure of distance from answering real briefs" is scoped to test wording, not to briefs; and the default ledger path is the real studio/knowledge/measurements.jsonl (1 row today), while gate 7 hashes only model_facts.jsonl — so stack_eval.py running the frozen brief set will append into the operator's live proposal queue and no gate notices.
findings.fix: Add `task` to the field list and derive it from the brief id. Point stack_eval.py at a fixture ledger via propose(path=...) and extend gate 7's before/after byte hash to measurements.jsonl and stack_runs.jsonl, not just model_facts.jsonl. State the queue metric as unique (model, attribute) pairs, since that is what the ledger actually deduplicates to.

findings.problem: score.py plans to embed third-party weights whose licence was never checked. I re-fetched huggingface.co/api/models?search=syncnet: lithiumice/syncnet and nawta/syncnet carry tags ['syncnet','s3fd','region:us'] — no license tag on either; the only licensed hit is the unrelated EEG braindecode/SyncNet (bsd-3-clause). The SyncNet/S3FD lineage is commonly research-only [UNVERIFIED — I did not read the upstream licence from here], which is precisely the case the pre-integration licence check exists for, and the section presents these two repos as the scorer without a word on it.
findings.fix: Read the licence from each candidate weight repo before session 4 and record it as a fact row with its quoted text; if it is non-commercial or research-only, stamp that on the scoring instrument and on any run record it produces, and say so in the proposal's risk block. If the licence cannot be established, that is could-not-measure and the weights do not get embedded.

findings.problem: The 535-page comfy walk is planned against an unstably-ordered list. My re-run of the exact URL the section quotes (limit=1&page=1&search=lipsync) confirms search is ignored (total 5345, totalPages 5345) but returned a DIFFERENT first record — muffins-flat-2-panoramic, not the comfyui-anyline the section reports. Ordering moves between runs (there is a search_ranking field and new nodes are being published; this one was created 2026-08-14), so a 535-request paged walk will duplicate some records and miss others, and a straight concatenation reads as a complete catalogue.
findings.fix: Dedupe the walk by node id, read `total` at the start and at the end, and report three numbers — pages walked, unique ids collected, total claimed — treating a mismatch as could-not-measure rather than as a catalogue.

findings.problem: The fail-loudly mitigation is written for the price parser only. fal.ai's HTML page is 317,743 bytes against fetch.py's 400,000 cap (79%), and the same page is also the source for the input schema (video_url, audio_url, guidance_scale, loop_mode). A truncation or redesign breaks the schema parse silently even if the '$' sentence is still found, and the section already admits it did not open fal.ai/api/openapi/queue/openapi.json this run and is relying on a recorded row for loop_mode.
findings.fix: Take the schema from the openapi JSON endpoint (structured and small) and keep the HTML fetch only for the price sentence; require both the byte count and the quoted sentence on the recorded fact, and fail loudly when the response length is within, say, 10% of the cap.

Section 5 — The ComfyUI ecosystem: knowi.section: Section 5 — The ComfyUI ecosystem: knowing every adapter, and what "can apply" is allowed to mean
Section 5 — The ComfyUI ecosystem: knowi.what_it_gets_right: Nearly every load-bearing number is reproducible, and I reproduced them rather than taking them: api.comfy.org total=5345 with the exact field shape; templates/index.json 603 templates / 601 with models / 603 minComfyUIVersion / openSource 225-325-53 / 168 distinct model names, all exact; model-list.json 287846 bytes in one fetch; Range answered 206 on raw.githubusercontent.com; the golden graph is 5 nodes with a bare-UUID subgraph type and a definitions block, carrying 6 bare model filenames. The negative finding on api.comfy.org/nodes/{id} (no model linkage) is the right kind of finding to lead with, and the section is built around it instead of around the brief's assumption. The fetch.py truncation defect is real in the tree (studio/mcp/fetch.py:392-408 reads max_bytes and returns PASS with no truncated field), headers is already a parameter (line 346) so fetch_all genuinely needs no second door, and advice.record (studio/mcp/advice.py:465-477) really does refuse a URL-contradicting vendor/portal/blog tier, so the tier gate rests on existing enforcement. Refused hosts were not re-probed or routed around, the 404 on a guessed template name is recorded as a self-inflicted error rather than a policy problem, and "can apply" is held to recorded-and-resolvable with execution pushed through scripts/measurement.py. The unmeasured items (per-graph parse rate across 603, the licence K baseline) are named as unmeasured.

findings.problem: Target state (2) hides that the majority of the joinable set is unclassified. The eight named classes sum to 187 on the shortlist (37+44+37+25+19+12+8+5), against 539 joinable — so roughly 65% land in `unclassified`, and that number appears nowhere in the definition of done. "539 of the 698 (77.2%) join to a declared node-class list" reads as capability coverage of 539 when the classified capability is 187. This is the Е3 case: an aggregate that reads as full work.
findings.fix: Add the unclassified count to the done criteria and print it alongside the eight: `classified 187, unclassified N, unjoinable 159 of 698`. Gate it the same way the class-with-zero-members rule is gated, so the unclassified bucket cannot grow silently as Comfy-Org adds node types the eight patterns do not match.

findings.problem: Gate 3's first negative control cannot go red. It proposes removing ".git-stripping and trailing-slash normalisation" and expects the join rate to drop. Measured on a 500-node registry sample just now: trailing slashes 0/500, `.git` suffixes 5/500 (~1%), but mixed case 433/500 (87%). Trailing-slash stripping is provably inert, and .git-stripping moves roughly 50 nodes out of 5345 — well inside a "tolerance band". The mutation the join actually depends on, lowercasing, is not the one the gate mutates.
findings.fix: Mutate the lowercase rule (drop it and the join should collapse by most of the 87% mixed-case rows), and assert the join counts as exact literals against the frozen fixture with no tolerance band — a frozen fixture is deterministic, so a band there only buys room for a regression to hide.

findings.problem: Gate 6 asserts something the existing ingest cannot express: that harvest rows carry "NO recorder-stated rung for api.comfy.org or raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/". scripts/ingest_harvest.py requires `tier` among its mandatory fields (line 169, checked against TIERS at 172) and passes it into advice.record, which refuses a blank tier outright. A row with no stated rung is rejected as malformed, not as a tier conflict — so the gate would pass for the wrong reason and prove nothing about the URL table.
findings.fix: State tier=portal on every emitted row and make the gate assert the enforcement that exists: advice.record must REFUSE a row for an api.comfy.org URL stated as vendor (verified behaviour, studio/mcp/advice.py:471-477), and source_hosts.classify must return the literal `portal` for both URL prefixes. Reword target-state/build claim "nothing in this pipeline states a rung" — the pipeline does state one; what it cannot do is override the table.

findings.problem: The `recorded-with-gaps` verdict frozen into gate 5 mislabels the case it is anchored on. The wan2.2 graph itself carries full resolvable HuggingFace URLs for the two lightx2v LoRAs (https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Wan_2.2_ComfyUI_Repackaged/resolve/main/split_files/loras/wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_{high,low}_noise.safetensors) — I read them out of widgets_values. They are absent from model-list.json, but they are not unresolvable. Freezing "gaps = these 2 names" as a golden literal bakes "missing from our catalogue" into a status that reads to a user as "you cannot get this file".
findings.fix: Resolve filenames against the graph's own URLs first and model-list.json second, and name the status after which source resolved it (e.g. resolvable-via-graph vs resolvable-via-catalogue vs unresolved). Re-anchor the golden test on a filename that resolves in neither.

findings.problem: The live half of gate 3 is a gate whose only failure mode is a number moving. The registry grows daily (the section itself records nodes created 2026-08-27 appearing mid-sweep) while extension-node-map.json is an unversioned file updated at Comfy-Org's discretion — so the 60.7% overall rate drifts downward for reasons that are not defects, and the band will be widened rather than investigated.
findings.fix: Keep the red on the frozen fixture only. On a live sweep, print `joined N of M` next to the sweep date and the previous sweep's figure, and fail only on a structural break the fixture test can characterise (zero joins, or a parse failure), not on drift.

findings.problem: Two reuse pointers do not survive opening the modules. studio/selfrag/cache.py is a PROMPT cache whose key is deliberately a fingerprint of the corpus, the model registry and the reflect rule table (it imports CorpusRecord, RULES, MODEL_CARDS); keying a fetched ComfyUI JSON blob on it means the catalogue cache is invalidated every time the prompt corpus changes, which is the opposite of the discipline being cited.
